adrs.title: UOR Mechanics — The Exact Math of Prime-Indexing
adrs.context: Mutable file-path identity permits duplication, reordering, and platform-dependent drift; UOR requires collision-free, compositionally rich, exactly reproducible identity across heterogeneous nodes.
adrs.decision: Adopt prime-indexing as the canonical UOR substrate. Irreducible identity: a prime is the invariant identity of a node; composites encode relations. Exponents as memory (OFA-ii): k_i in n = product p_i^k_i is a surplus ledger; primes accumulate monotonically (p to p^2 to p^3). Lawful composition: K1 ⊗ K2 = lcm(K1, K2) as a lossless structural join preventing duplication. Multiplicative union: K1 ⊕ K2 = product over p of p^(v_p(K1) + v_p(K2)). Zero-drift architecture: exact rational arithmetic only, no floating point. Cryptographic verification: Binary Canonical Serialization (fixed field orders, ULEB128 prefixes) and Poseidon2 ZK sealing (t=9, r=8). Call-market cleavage (Holotrade, phase-gated): Fee = 1/10 * DeltaP; node yield = ask + 9/10 * DeltaP, with receipt-locked ledger finality.
consequences: State is never identified by mutable path; one prime-indexed ledger drives identity, history, and compensation
Merges are lossless and deduplicating (lcm); unions are exact (exponent addition)
BCS + Poseidon2 sealing make receipts tamper-evident and cross-platform (Rust/Lean)
Banned floats foreclose drift and penny-shaving settlement attacks

adrs.title: Symmetry-Matched Polarization Analysis in MnF2
adrs.context: Unpolarized inelastic neutron scattering on MnF2 reported no resolvable altermagnetic magnon band splitting within resolution, while polarized INS later accessed an antisymmetric dynamical channel and reported a domain-dependent chiral response: different measurement operations, not contradictions. A null in one channel must not be treated as physical absence in another.
adrs.decision: Adopt symmetry-matched polarization analysis as the interpretive discipline for altermagnetic neutron-scattering claims in MnF2: decompose the transverse dynamical magnetic correlation tensor via the Blume-Maleev cross section into polarization-even and odd parts so that reversing incident neutron polarization isolates the antisymmetric (chiral) correlator; classify nulls into the four-null taxonomy (physical, resolution, polarization-projection, antiferromagnetic-domain cancellation), deliberately contextual rather than exhaustive; require a resolvability criterion that states which channel each null belongs to and declares the anti-ferromagnetic domain state for domain-sensitive readout.
consequences: Unpolarized null results are located in the taxonomy rather than overruling polarized signatures
Spectral resolution and chiral sensitivity are kept as separate design axes
Every null claim carries an explicit stage of loss, making comparisons falsifiable
Provides the channel separation on which the dJ7 source-sector, reversal-space and probe-tensor work items build

adrs.title: The dJ7 Principle - Symmetry-Complement Source Sectors in Altermagnetic MnF2
adrs.context: A Hamiltonian term small in total energy can be leading in a selected symmetry channel. In MnF2 a small imbalance between the two symmetry-distinct seventh-neighbor Heisenberg exchange bonds (J7a, J7b) is a candidate source coordinate for the altermagnetic chiral response; whether the construction is valid depends on a precise group-theoretic statement relative to a declared reference model.
adrs.decision: Adopt the dJ7 principle as the canonical account of symmetry-complement source sectors in altermagnetic MnF2: group averaging over a reference group G0 defines a projector onto the invariant subspace and splits V = im P XOR ker P into invariant sector and symmetry-complement source sector; a coefficient lambda in the complement obeys the covariance F_O(rho_s lambda) = chi_O(s) F_O(lambda), and under rho_s = -I the odd response has only odd total degree F(lambda) = k*lambda + O(||lambda||^3) (selection, not amplification); the source is the inequivalence dJ7 = J7b - J7a of the seventh-neighbor bonds with the bond-label convention declared explicitly; the result is a bounded-range-seven near-scalar, not a universal one-dimensional coordinate.
consequences: Source attribution is tied to a declared reference model and bond convention, preventing tautological complement definitions
The odd-channel expansion fixes the scaling of the chiral response, enabling falsifiability
Substrate for reversal-space tomography and probe-tensor correspondence
Explicitly warns against exporting dJ7 as a universal weak coordinate to other altermagnets

adrs.title: When Null Does Not Mean Absent - Measurement-Map Geometry and Null-Witness Duality

adrs.decision: Adopt the layered measurement-map geometry with null-witness duality: factor the total map M = T A P R S over source/state, response, probe projection, ensemble/domain averaging, and transfer/resolution; define observational equivalence by measurement fibers; in a layered linear experiment with cumulative maps Fj record the cumulative null filtration Kj = ker Fj and dual witness spaces Wj = Ann(Kj) = im Fj*; treat the total observational quotient as factorization-independent while stage-local null attribution is invariant only under invertible reparameterizations of declared intermediate spaces, not under arbitrary refactorization; a target C is identifiable after stage j iff Kj is subset of ker C with obstruction dimension dC(A) = dim C(ker A); passive post-processing cannot restore an erased distinction, whereas active intervention creates a new measurement map; combine independent probes by kernel intersection only under a common latent state; extend to nonlinear/noisy (nuisance-projected Jacobians, Fisher information), stochastic (outcome distributions), and quantum (POVM probability maps) measurements.
consequences: Every null is attributed to a declared stage or its label is withheld
A large raw signal can be non-identifying while a null channel coexists with a nonzero orthogonal-sector signal
Upstream source contradiction is distinct from a downstream projection null
Reversal channels double as obstruction testbeds

adrs.title: Target-First Observability Calculus - Admissible Ambiguity and Dual Obstructions
adrs.context: Experimental design is often organized around an available instrument rather than the claim the data support. A high-amplitude measurement can have zero target design gain while a much smaller measurement exactly closes the target; design must work backward from the claim.
adrs.decision: Adopt the target-first observability calculus: specify the target, prerequisite state, and state gate before the forward map; for exact common-state linear measurements define residual structural ambiguity OC(E) = C(ker AE) with closure when {0}, structural design gain DeltaC(B|E) = dC(E) - dC(E union B) >= 0, and report exact closure separately from admissible-set contraction OC(E; y, Omega) with width wC; any v in ker AE with Cv != 0 is a constructive dual counterexample, and the most useful next experiment is one maximally sensitive to it; place the target in an allowed parity sector while recording model-forbidden sectors as obstruction channels; after structural viability, optimize practical margin with nuisance-projected Jacobians (c-optimal / goal-oriented OED downstream); enforce the rule that a downstream response cannot repair a contradicted upstream source state; publish per-claim target, state gate, forward map, nuisance variables, an explicit target-changing ambiguity, reversal/complementary probe, conditioning diagnostic, and an attempted falsification.
consequences: Experiment selection is justified by target design gain or contraction, not raw amplitude
Exact closure and quantitative contraction are reported separately
A 13-step protocol governs claim production and publication

For MnF2 three shortcuts are forbidden: magnon splitting alone does not identify signed exchange; a chiral signal does not by symmetry determine static multipole rank; a static multipole reconstruction does not prove another probe's dynamical response

adrs.title: UOR Civic Infrastructure
adrs.context: The Foundry DAO progresses through three strategic developmental epochs. PrismPM governs process and packaging law; the UCC governs physical and dynamical law via the universal closure sextuple. PWEH operationalizes contractivity and fail-closed interlocks as an active execution lock, and CRMF envelopes canonicalized under BCS provide tamper-evident attestation. The architecture requires a canonical wire format for cryptographic commitments, a fail-closed governance mechanism, and an integrity chain that binds execution traces to prime-indexed attestations.
adrs.decision: Adopt the canonical BCS wire format for the UnsignedCrmfEnvelope, the PWEH integrity binding for execution traces, the contractivity gate for the UCC, and fail-closed interlocks for governance.
consequences: Deterministic, cross-language canonical byte streams for cryptographic commitments (Rust/Lean reproducible)
Path-dependent tamper resistance across the whole PWEH chain
Fail-closed governance: any unmodeled defect halts L0 before side effects materialize
Poseidon2 sponge absorption is the ZK sealing stage
Floating-point is structurally excluded from all wire formats (ADR-0021)

adrs.context: Artifact transitions lack a fail-closed governance gate: a semantic proof may compile while the lifted manifold violates the Banach fixed-point contractivity bound, or execution drift may exceed its allowance.
adrs.decision: Adopt the PrismPM/PIRTM synthesis: transitions are admitted by the ACE veto gate only when PrismPM semantic proofs are dischargeable AND the lifted gain matrix is strictly contractive (rho(Λ) < 1 − ε in fixed-point scaled units) AND drift stays within its bounded allowance. Add and Multiply map onto the prime-indexed tensor overlay as p=2 and p=3.

Deterministic scaled-integer comparisons make the gate symbolically model-checkable
Universal BCS packing yields a replay-injective ensemble manifest wire format
Phase D resumption binds the BCS gap seal in a dual-authority signed request (K1 != K2)

adrs.title: PrismPm Archivum
adrs.context: Governance receipts must persist as immutable, versioned, and traceable artifacts that survive runtime execution and are queryable during audit.
adrs.decision: Adopt the Prime-Indexed Archivum (Λ^p-Archivum) storage layer as the canonical permanent repository for the active governance pipeline: CRMF seals CrmfEventEnvelope records under the active domain tag, the Compatible() fail-closed gate admits only same-domain envelopes, and every validated envelope is appended to a hash-linked, append-only non-WORM ledger keyed under Blake3-derived primes. Legacy WORM storage is superseded by this active cryptographic topology.
consequences: Governance receipts persist as immutable, versioned, traceable artifacts queryable during audit (hash-chain + prime index)
Cross-domain or tag-mismatched envelopes are vetoed at the Compatible() gate before any storage (fail-closed)
Append-only integrity is enforced by a hash-chained ledger; tamper evidence is machine-checked (Lean + Kani)
Every accepted ADR retains a reconstructible provenance path (traceability invariant)

adrs.title: OSCAL and PrismPM
adrs.context: PrismPM transforms .lex.tex models into verified artifacts, while enterprise compliance requires standardized reporting such as NIST OSCAL. If the compliance narrative were computed or negotiated independently of the settled mathematical execution, a contractivity/drift breach (SIG_GOV_KILL) could be reported as an accepted state. The P²C Core v1.1 Witness Calculus mandate forbids this: calculations are the sole domain of the physical execution engine, and compliance must be a consequence of exact arithmetic, not a sociologically negotiated paper trail.
adrs.decision: Adopt the Legalese Scopist as the exclusive, read-only translation mapping layer downstream of PrismPM and the Sedona Spine. It ingests the cryptographically sealed ContractivityReceipt R emitted when artifacts are evaluated, applies the deterministic mapping f_Scopist(R) = Narrative_legal to produce an OSCAL assessment-result model, and is mathematically forbidden from recalculating, negotiating, or re-interpreting risk. OSCAL is packaging-only (an optional read-only export envelope, never a runtime attester); any OSCAL Assessment Result (SAR) lacking a hashed R1CS compiler manifest or Lean proof hash must explicitly mark its evidence as UNATTESTED. The Scopist law is enforced inside an axiom-clean Lean 4 core.
consequences: Zero-drift enforcement: a SIG_GOV_KILL verdict always yields an UNATTESTED narrative — the legal layer cannot mitigate a kill
Deterministic translation: identical receipts (same lift id, norm Psi_+, Delta, proof hash, verdict) produce identical narratives (idempotency & purity)
Packaging-only OSCAL: risk is copied verbatim from the receipt (never recalculated); OSCAL is a read-only narrative envelope, never a runtime attester
Unattested markings: an SAR lacking a hashed R1CS compiler manifest or Lean proof hash is explicitly marked UNATTESTED
Negative: rigorous schema alignment between PrismPM model definitions and the Scopist mapping is mandatory to prevent translation failures

adrs.title: Native Textual Typing and Operator-Class Constraint
adrs.context: The temporal-operator class G_time of the Langlands Prism program must be grounded in a reproducible, native-corpus certification. The typing vector T(l) = (TFSI, GESI, AspectVar, DepDepth, AdjRank, Morphology) must be computed from the native Hebrew (Masoretic) and Aramaic (Peshitta) corpora with full vocalization retained, no English transliteration at any stage, and clause boundaries determined by native punctuation and syntax (never by translation or human judgment). Section 9 of the certification protocol separates corpus certification from operator certification: only the left half C -> T(l) -> T(G) is certified; operator assignment Gamma, representation rho, and the claim tau(l) in G belong to Section 10. Without a hardened, falsifiable typing constraint, an operator-class assignment could be adopted without any possibility of rejection.
adrs.decision: Certify the native textual typing constraint via the reproducible Section 9 pipeline: deterministic clause-boundary and F1-F4 frame rules, the clause graph G_C, the four null models (lemma shuffle, morphology-preserving shuffle, clause-order shuffle, dependency-tree permutation) to estimate each threshold theta_X as the 95th percentile over the training split only, thresholds frozen before test evaluation; Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.01; and the hard, falsifiable control-separation criterion N inter T(G_time) = empty plus P_T union P_G subset T(G_time) on the held-out split. Adopt the exclusion test T(l) not-in T(G) implies tau(l) not-in G as the framework's falsifiability condition. Section 9 certifies only C -> T(l) -> T(G); operator assignment, representations, and claims are deferred to Section 10.
consequences: Certification boundary: Section 9 certifies only the reproducible computation of T(l) from the native corpus; Gamma, rho, and tau(l) in G are Section 10 deliverables, never certified here
Falsifiability: a representation assignment can be rejected without requiring an alternative interpretation to be accepted (exclusion test)
Hard control separation: N inter T(G_time) = empty and P_T union P_G subset T(G_time); failure of either condition forces revision of F, G_C, or the thresholds
No physics, no transliteration, no human judgment: all typing coordinates are native textual statistics
Frozen artifacts: corpus and analyzer version hashes and thresholds are frozen before test evaluation; multiple-testing correction at q = 0.01

adrs.title: Meta-Relativity F1
adrs.context: Meta-Relativity is a bounded-operator calculus with arithmetic labels on the prime-gated Hilbert space ℋ = ℓ²(𝔓) ⊗ L²(ℝ) ⊗ ℂᵈ with 𝒰 = A + B + E, prime kernel K_pq = p^(-α)q^(-α)h(log p − log q) (α > 1/2, Hilbert–Schmidt), an almost-periodic Fourier multiplier and a finite self-adjoint block Ξ; lifts strongly commute, the spectrum is a Minkowski sum and σ_ess(𝒰) = σ(A) + EssRan(m) + σ(E) with σ_ess(A) = {0}. The Stage-1 certificate on P = 25 was executed with A = D_σ + K: the previously-proposed ℓ² vector scaling undershot the operator-norm budget (η = 1.1 looked like a pass), the separate ‖K‖ triangle bound is vacuous on every cell (‖K‖₂ ≈ 0.163 > floor), and the earlier over-claim that 'the locked CPTP block passes MR' was retracted — sharp Weyl sees the bottom, the cap ‖Ξ‖ ≤ 1 is a spread constraint, and a cap-respecting lift of the Lindblad pair is a declared construction, not a theorem. The SBM/F1 wall-to-zero branch certifies only Δ_V (the same-sign-locked |C_expl − ∫W·arg ζ| = |S|); Δ_{N,T} is a Hadamard-tail diagnostic. The Section 9 analogy holds as certified exclusion.
adrs.decision: Declare the certified MR core and its Stage-1 certificate rule: declare (α, σ, η, P), scale B and E in operator norm, pass iff η < 1 with GapLB = (1−η)·p_max^(-σ), reject at η ≥ 1 (the rejection is conservative: reject ≠ indefinite). Fold K into A = D_σ + K; never certificate against the separated ‖K‖ form. Keep Meta-Relativity as written as the default window: cap ‖Ξ‖ ≤ 1 on, raw locked H = diag(0, γ₁…γ₈) (γ₈ = 43.327) inadmissible; a shrink is allowed only if declared as part of the window; sharp-cap-off is a different, named object without essential-spectrum claims. Do not license τ(היה) = 𝒰 (Section 9 typing does not determine the representation). Do not compose MR with SBM/F1/CPTP/Section 9 without the explicit map h = φ * Reζ(½ + i·) and HS/sign checks. Keep Δ_V as the only SBM object; keep Δ_{N,T} in the diagnostic appendix and never cite it as zero-free evidence, never scan it to b = 1/2, never define arg ζ by a partial sum without an explicit-formula remainder. Do not run Stage 2/3 until Δ_V is mesh-stable. Keep the two corrections attached to the freeze: g(z) uses c² − (z−b)², and C_expl(½; 3/2, 7/2) = (π/20) log(18π²/245) ≈ −0.05049.
consequences: Stage-1 certificate rule: declare (α, σ, η, P), scale in operator norm; η < 1 passes with GapLB = (1−η)·p_max^(-σ); η ≥ 1 rejects the certificate — and rejection is conservative, it never claims U is indefinite.
Operator-norm budget lock: ‖B‖ + ‖E‖ = η·p_max^(-σ) exactly; ℓ²-of-the-diagonal vector scaling undershoots the budget and is rejected.
Folding correction: A = D_σ + K, not K; the separate-‖K‖ triangle bound is vacuous on every cell (‖K‖₂ ≈ 0.163 > floor at α = 1.5); λ_min(A) equals the floor p_max^(-σ) to a part in 10³.

Sharp Weyl separates bottom from spread: λ_min(Ξ) controls the bottom, ‖Ξ‖₂ controls the σ_ess spread. MR-written keeps cap ‖Ξ‖ ≤ 1: raw locked H inadmissible; declared shrinks allowed; sharp-cap-off is a different named object with no essential-spectrum claims.
Primes are data and the inequality is analysis: GapLB is a theorem about operator norms, not about primes; K adds parts in 10³ at the bottom and does not open the gap.
Boundary not-list: not RH, not Hilbert–Pólya, not det_reg(I−Θ⁻ˢ) = ξ(s), not special relativity, not the finite Arakelov Hodge index, not a license to set τ(היה) = 𝒰.
No composition without the explicit map h = φ * Reζ(½ + i·) plus Hilbert–Schmidt and sign checks; MR commutes as citation with SBM/F1/CPTP/Section 9 only.
Stage 1 locked: (c,d) = (3/2, 7/2), b > 1, empty S, Simpson vs closed form, errors inside the tail, 10⁻⁵ budget; if the table ever breaks, stop — the branch or the weight is wrong.

Stage 2 (b ∈ (1/2, 1)) and Stage 3 (scan to 1/2) are not run; Δ_{N,T} is a Hadamard-tail meter, never zero-free evidence, never scanned to 1/2, never a surrogate for arg ζ; Δ_V = |C_expl − ∫W·arg ζ| = |S| is the only SBM object.
P-scale stability: (α, σ, η) = (1.5, 0.5, 0.5) passes at P = 25/50/100; ‖K‖₂ is frozen at 0.163 by the small primes while the floor falls as p_max^(-σ).
Freeze corrections: g(z) uses c² − (z−b)² (not c − (z−b)²); the collapsed SBM example dropped a π, giving C_expl(½; 3/2, 7/2) = (π/20)·log(18π²/245) ≈ −0.05049.
